items_missed: No 'How are you today?' at the open.

Estimate likely under-quoted. She quoted 3-4 hours / $612-$816, which is BELOW the 3.5-5.5 hour typical range she had just cited for a two-bedroom - despite a 9th-floor origin where the customer confirmed the building will not reserve the elevator. Shared-elevator wait time on nine floors is a real overage risk and it was not priced in.
The unreservable elevator was acknowledged ('no worries') but never converted into a time or cost variable for the customer.
No visual equivalent used to help him picture scope or truck capacity (school bus reference or similar).

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing - no 'prep shortens the move and lowers your bill', no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip. Especially costly on a 9th-floor elevator move where staging items by the door is the single biggest time saver.
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email.
Never gave business hours or how to reach the company (she did give hours on her other call this day).
Insurance explanation covered No Worries but not the 60 cents/lb baseline - and the customer specifically raised the $2,000 coverage himself, so the door was open.
top_strength: Real ownership on the date change - when he asked to move from Saturday the 22nd to Sunday the 23rd she actively checked every branch's availability rather than just declining, then offered Monday the 24th and saved the booking. She also did genuine diligence on logistics, pulling up the map herself to verify street parking at the destination and mapping exactly which items were going to the second floor.
coaching_note: Two fixes, in order of value: add the Save Your Ass prep speech (10 points, and it directly protects the estimate), and stop discounting the elevator risk. A 9th-floor origin with a non-reservable elevator should push the estimate up toward the 4-5.5 hour range, not below the 3.5-hour floor - quoting 3-4 hours here is the kind of under-quote that shows up later as a blown estimate.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and genuinely responsive - 'no worries', 'glad to hear that', absorbed his rambling item list patiently, used his name three times, and went out of her way on the date change and the parking check.
